continuation_prompts: A realistic cinematic Polish historical drama inside a Warsaw shop in the 1880s. The camera stands at the end of a polished wooden counter. On the left a middle-aged man in a dark coat and top hat, Wokulski, the shop owner; on the right a young woman in a dark green dress and a feathered hat, Izabela. Both have turned toward the camera so that their two faces are fully visible in three-quarter view, heads up, eyes open, softly lit from the shop window, while they talk quietly about a letter lying on the counter. Keep the same two faces, the same positions, clothing, counter, letter and lighting throughout. Steady eye-level camera, one continuous take, no cuts, no new prominent people. The two characters take turns speaking natural, clearly pronounced Polish in a calm, intimate tone, answering each other promptly with small natural head, eye and hand movements and realistic expressions; the listener reacts quietly. Soft shop ambience under the voices: the low murmur of customers further back, footsteps on wooden floors, a clock ticking. No subtitles, no text, no music. Wokulski, the man: <d>[Polish] To list od pani Nowakowej. Jej córce odmówiono pracy w moim sklepie.</d> Izabela, the woman: <d>[Polish] Czy zna pan powód? Nie chciałabym nikogo osądzać pochopnie.</d> Wokulski, the man: <d>[Polish] Ja też nie. Dlatego pytam panią.</d>
